We've got to look at carbon capture technologies that would draw carbon back from the atmosphere. Some of those could be natural, like trees and restoration of natural systems in the ocean. Some of those could be engineered, like direct air capture. We've got to look at a pricing mechanism for carbon so that we send the right price signals to the economy. And then we've got to deal with short-lived climate pollutants. And at the same time, We do all that mitigation. We've got to deal with adaptation. We've got to get ready for the effects of climate change that we know are coming, whether those are intense different periods of drought, sea level rise, or whatever those might be. There's a lot of jobs opportunities in those things. It's true. This is not a jobs program, but there's going to be a lot of investment. And then I think the other orientation we have to have is that it's as taxpayers, it's much more expensive to wait till this happens to us. for us to invest now and get ahead of it. So very much like COVID, if you just spend a little bit of money on preventing COVID, you could have saved a ton of money in responding to it. Climate's going to be that many, many times over. So the idea of the climate playbook is let's figure out all these actions we have to take. Every congressional committee has essentially has a role, whether you're talking about agriculture or tax breaks at ways and means or you know, regulating oil and gas at energy and commerce, but we need to get working on it.
